analysis.title: GS Equities: Sector Sentiment + Standouts | September Edition (1 Oct 2026)
key_insights: TMT desk: the most debated topics are agentic commerce (impact of personal assistants), DASH/SPOT/ABNB/TTWO, CPUs, semicap versus memory, EDA software, and PANW/CRWD. META had its best month since July 2013 on product momentum via Muse, and the inference economy (capex-light ways to play AI, such as data infrastructure and cyber names) kept trending.

TMT catalysts for October: SEMICON West (10/13-15), NVDA GTC Berlin (10/20-22), and the start of Q3 earnings toward month-end. The desk will watch hyperscaler revenue and cloud margins for the broader AI trade.
TMT 14-day RSI screen: oversold INTU, BILL, LFTO, TTWO, ZG, COMP, CHTR, NU, TTD, TCOM, PAYX. Overbought DDOG, TWLO, OKTA, DT, META, ASML, AMD, TSM.

Financials desk: the main debates are V and MA positioning on agentic payments, HOOD (product velocity and prediction markets versus valuation), FICO/EFX/TRU (FICO versus Vantage share and a possible move away from tri-merge), ALLY (net interest margin and credit), and CBOE (SPX contract renewal, perpetual futures, tokenization).

Financials: higher rates were the biggest inflection, weighing on capital markets activity. Catalysts are big-bank earnings starting 10/13 and the October FOMC. Oversold: BAC, RF, BNY, ALLY, SF, BX, FIS, AON, FICO, NMIH. Overbought: COIN, MRX, HOOD.

Healthcare desk: topical names are MRNA, MRK, TMO, HUM, BSX and TWST. The inflection was TMO walking through its long-range plan at a competitor's conference. Catalysts are Medicare Advantage STARs scores and ESMO data on the MRNA/MRK cancer vaccine. Tools multiples look extended.

Consumer desk: sentiment worsened on companies with heavy European exposure (especially apparel, with RL named) and on the low-income consumer after comments at the GS Retail conference about a widening K-shaped economy. Cruise bookings stayed strong despite geopolitical and macro concerns.

Consumer: off-price retail (TJX, BURL) is under structural debate over why trends are not better. High-frequency data is the largest correlate of stock direction, with recent improvement at BURL, GAP and AEO. Oil (freight and margins in 2027) and rates (housing and autos) are the next focus.

Consumer extension screen: upside SG, GME, OLLI, SIG, GAP, MAR. Downside MGM, TXRH, BROS, SFD, FRPT. Agentic AI dominated client questions for two weeks, but core consumer stocks have been largely immune, with weakness concentrated in internet, pockets of financials and business services.

Industrials desk: investors are in a holding pattern driven by the Middle East, oil, rates and midterms, and the desk expects cyclicals to remain for sale until there is clarity. Industrials inflected lower broadly and trade at 1 and 5 year lows versus the market, with sentiment souring in AI/data center, short cycle, aerospace and transports.

Industrials catalysts: ISM, truck orders, auto sales and Q3 earnings, where topline strength competes with price/cost headwinds. Conference updates from JBHT, CARR and LECO suggest price/cost may be a widespread Q3 headwind. Oversold: WY, ADT, GD, AN, LHX. Overbought: KEYS, ZBRA, NDSN, AME, CCL.

Energy and utilities desk: refiner 3Q revisions screen bullish, but more specialists are cautious on valuation, policy controls and demand destruction with diesel at highs (VLO, MPC, PBF, DK, DINO). Concern about diesel export bans, quotas and tariffs raised the rate-of-change worry for a group still +130% YTD versus XLE +38%.

Gas midstream (KMI, WMB, DTM, TRP): rates remain a headwind and most stocks broke their 200-day levels in September. Energy earnings start mid-October, with focus on oilfield services guidance (international downtime versus North American pricing power) and E&P capex step-ups and production revisions given elevated crude.

Energy extension screen: oversold WMB, DTM, CCJ, FSLR, EXE, HAL, WFRD. Overbought CVI, SEI, MUR, REP, VLO, PBF. A potential diesel export ban was the most topical story on the desk, with strong inbound interest from generalists and specialists.

Special situations desk: MGM Resorts is reportedly discussing a proposal to acquire People Inc (PPLI), one day after PPLI walked away from its $48.30/shr proposal for MGM, and MGM shares fell. Regulatory-path debates cover NSC/UNP, LNTH (HSR) and ZIM.

Merger-arb catalysts in October: KVUE/KMB (EU Phase I), AES (EU FSR and Phase I), LNTH (HSR refiled), PSNL (HSR), D/NE (VA PUC hearing), AXTA (EU FSR). Most popular arb names are KVUE/KMB, NSC/UNP, AES, ROKU/FOXA and CZR.

Corporate donations to state attorneys general associations (RAGA and DAGA) set records, with a combined $37 million in the first half of 2026 and about 90% of contributions from corporations, per a WSJ analysis.

sector_views.rationale: Desk expects cyclicals to remain for sale until the Middle East, oil, rates and midterms clear. Industrials trade at 1 and 5 year lows versus the market.
Sentiment is worse on the low-income consumer and European-exposed apparel, while cruise bookings are strong and core consumer stocks have been relatively insulated from agentic AI concerns.
3Q revisions screen bullish, but specialists are tilting cautious on valuation, policy controls and demand destruction with diesel at highs.
Rates are a headwind and most stocks broke their 200-day levels in September, with debate over valuation and near-term catalysts.

earnings_insights: Big banks start Q3 earnings on 10/13, and the broader Q3 season kicks off toward month-end. No figures are given.
Industrials Q3 earnings: the battle is topline strength versus price/cost headwinds and macro uncertainty. JBHT, CARR and LECO conference updates point to a widespread price/cost headwind.
Energy earnings begin mid-October. Focus is FY guidance updates for oilfield services and capex or production revisions for E&Ps given elevated crude. Refiner 3Q revisions screen bullish.
Hyperscaler Q3 revenue and cloud margins are the key read for the broader AI trade.

CBOE is debating perpetual futures and tokenization alongside its SPX contract renewal.
risk_factors: Middle East conflict, oil prices, rates and midterms keep cyclical investors on the sidelines.
Diesel export bans, quotas and tariffs, and demand destruction with diesel at highs, threaten refiners.
Price/cost headwinds and rising macro uncertainty threaten industrial Q3 earnings.

A widening K-shaped economy is hurting the low-income consumer.
Regulatory outcomes are the key risk for NSC/UNP, ZIM and LNTH.
